verdicts.flaw_description: A named alternative cause reaches every unit: "Every shop refitted its machines with a faster insert grade that quarter, and every logged run was cut on one of those machines" - so the 4-7 minute reductions are equally explained by the new insert grade rather than the coolant.

Two of the four cases measure the outcome before the intervention: case One was "issued 4 November" but scored "by 27 September", and case Three was "issued 5 June" but scored "by 28 April". The effect precedes the cause in half the evidence.

The measure covers a narrower population than the claim: "Figures cover the orders that cleared the staffed tills, and about a fifth of each store's orders went through self-checkout", so revenue per order is computed on ~80% of orders selected by checkout channel, not on all orders as the claim requires.

Absence is measured only on a subset that excludes the pupils most likely to be absent: figures "cover the pupils enrolled for the whole term, and about a fifth of each cohort left part-way through", so the 4-7 percent drops are computed on a survivor population narrower than the cohort the claim is about.
